title: Andaman Islands vs Maldives: Which Should You Visit?
description: Andaman Islands vs Maldives — a data-backed comparison based on Reddit discussions, real costs, and traveler preferences. Honest verdicts for your next trip.

categories.title: 💰 Cost of Travel
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands are a clear winner for budget travelers. A comfortable daily budget, including decent accommodation, food, and a couple of activities, can range from ₹3,000 to ₹6,000 ($35-$70 USD) per person. You can find guesthouses in Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) for ₹1,500-₹3,000 ($18-$36), local meals for ₹200-₹500 ($2.5-$6), and activities like snorkeling for ₹1,000-₹2,000 ($12-$24). In stark contrast, the Maldives often demand $300-$1000+ USD per day for resort stays, with even budget guesthouses on local islands like Maafushi starting at $70-$150. Food on resorts is typically $50-$100 per meal. "Seriously, the diving in Havelock for what I paid felt like a steal compared to what my friend dropped in Thailand, let alone the Maldives." This sums up the value proposition perfectly.

winnerSummary.why: The Andaman Islands offer an incredible travel experience at a fraction of the cost of the Maldives, making it accessible to a much wider range of budgets.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Budget travelers, backpackers, families, and anyone looking for maximum value without compromising on natural beauty.

categories.title: 🏖️ Beaches & Scenery
categories.summary: While both destinations boast stunning beaches, the Maldives takes the crown for its sheer consistent perfection and the iconic overwater bungalow aesthetic. The powder-soft white sand and impossibly clear, warm lagoons of virtually every Maldivian island, whether a private resort or a local gem like Fulidhoo, are unparalleled. Beaches like Radhanagar Beach in Havelock (Andamans) are breathtaking and often less crowded, offering a more rugged, natural beauty, but the manicured, dreamlike quality of Maldivian resorts and their surrounding waters is a cut above for the 'paradise' feel. The coral reefs directly accessible from many Maldivian resorts also offer an immediate underwater spectacle that requires more effort to find in some parts of the Andamans. "My honeymoon in the Maldives felt like living inside a postcard; every single view was just unreal, like a perfect painting." The curated experience is key here.

winnerSummary.why: The Maldives offers a consistent, iconic, and meticulously maintained 'paradise' beach experience that is globally unmatched.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Luxury travelers, honeymooners, photographers, and those seeking the quintessential 'paradise island' aesthetic.

categories.title: 🐠 Activities & Excursions
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer a more diverse range of activities that cater to adventurous spirits. Beyond incredible scuba diving in places like Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep) where PADI certifications can be obtained for ₹20,000-₹28,000 ($240-$335), you can explore historical landmarks like the Cellular Jail in Port Blair, trek through lush rainforests, and witness bioluminescence at night. You can also visit active mud volcanoes on Baratang Island, which is a unique experience. The Maldives focuses heavily on water-based activities like snorkeling and diving (also world-class), but often at premium prices. A single resort dive can be $100-$150. While luxury experiences abound, the variety beyond the aquatic realm is limited. "Andamans was epic, we dove with manta rays, explored old British ruins, and even saw a mud volcano, all in one trip!" The breadth of experiences makes Andamans a winner.

winnerSummary.why: The Andaman Islands provide a richer variety of activities spanning adventure, history, and nature, beyond just water sports.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Adventure seekers, history buffs, active travelers, and those who enjoy a diverse itinerary.

categories.title: 🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: When it comes to accommodation, the Maldives is in a league of its own for luxury and unique experiences. The sheer number of world-class resorts, each on its own island, offering everything from opulent beach villas to iconic overwater bungalows (starting from $400-$2000+ per night), is unmatched. Resorts like W Maldives or Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru set global standards for luxury and privacy. While the Andaman Islands have lovely mid-range resorts like Barefoot at Havelock or Taj Exotica Resort & Spa, Andamans, they don't offer the same level of architectural grandeur, exclusivity, or the signature Maldivian overwater experience. Andaman accommodations are more focused on comfort and blending with nature, often simpler and more rustic. "Staying in an overwater villa in the Maldives was literally a dream come true, you wake up and jump straight into the ocean!" That experience is unique.

winnerSummary.why: The Maldives offers an unparalleled range of luxury accommodations, particularly the iconic overwater bungalows, which are a destination in themselves.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Luxury travelers, honeymooners, those seeking unique and high-end resort experiences.

categories.title: 🍽️ Food & Dining
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands win for a more authentic and diverse culinary experience, especially for foodies who love fresh seafood and Indian flavors. Port Blair and Havelock offer numerous local shacks and restaurants serving delicious, freshly caught seafood thalis (₹300-₹600 / $3.5-$7), crab curry, and a variety of Indian and Bengali dishes. Must-try spots include Something Different – A Beachside Café in Havelock for ambiance and fresh catch, or Annapurna Restaurant in Port Blair for local Indian fare. In the Maldives, while resorts offer high-quality international cuisine, often with Michelin-star chefs, the dining is generally curated and expensive. A single meal can easily cost $50-$100, and local Maldivian food (like Garudhiya or Mashuni) is harder to find outside of local islands or specific Maldivian-themed nights at resorts. "Honestly, the fresh grilled fish in Andamans was some of the best I've ever had, and for so cheap! You can't beat that authenticity." It's about flavor and value.

winnerSummary.why: The Andaman Islands offer a more authentic, diverse, and significantly more affordable culinary journey centered around fresh seafood and local flavors.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Foodies, budget travelers, those who appreciate local cuisine, and seafood lovers.

categories.title: ✈️ Getting There
categories.summary: Getting to both destinations involves flights, but the logistics differ. To the Andaman Islands, you first need to fly into a major Indian city like Chennai (MAA), Bengaluru (BLR), or Kolkata (CCU), then take a domestic flight (approx. 2-2.5 hours, ₹4,000-₹8,000 / $48-$96) to Port Blair (IXZ). From Port Blair, government or private ferries (like Makruzz or Green Ocean, ₹500-₹1,500 / $6-$18) take you to Havelock or Neil Island. The Maldives, on the other hand, often has direct international flights from major global cities to Malé (MLE). However, once you land, you'll need a pre-arranged seaplane (often $300-$600 round trip) or speedboat transfer to your specific resort island, adding significant cost and sometimes waiting time. "Flying into Malé was easy, but that seaplane transfer cost almost as much as my flight from Dubai!" Both have their quirks; one requires an internal flight, the other an expensive final leg.

winnerSummary.why: Both destinations have similar travel times from major international hubs, though the internal connections and costs differ significantly after the initial flight.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Travelers prioritizing convenience (Maldives) vs. those willing for an extra domestic leg for value (Andamans).

categories.title: 🚗 Getting Around
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer far more flexibility and independence in getting around. On islands like Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep), you can easily rent a scooter for ₹400-₹600 ($5-$7) per day, allowing you to explore at your own pace, discover hidden beaches, and visit local eateries. Auto-rickshaws are also readily available and affordable for shorter distances. Inter-island travel is covered by government and private ferries. In the Maldives, movement is largely restricted to your resort island and pre-arranged transfers. Resort guests rely on speedboats or seaplanes provided by their resort (often included in the package or a hefty add-on). On local islands like Maafushi, you can walk or rent a bicycle, but you can't freely explore other islands without booking expensive excursions. "Renting a scooter in Havelock and finding my own little beach spots was a highlight; you just don't get that freedom in the Maldives." This autonomy gives Andamans the edge.

winnerSummary.why: The Andaman Islands offer significantly more freedom and affordable options for independent exploration within and between islands.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Independent travelers, adventurers, and those who enjoy self-guided exploration.

categories.title: 🎭 Culture & Local Experience
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer a much richer and more accessible cultural experience. Port Blair, the capital, is steeped in history with the Cellular Jail (tickets ~₹30 / $0.35) providing a sobering insight into India's struggle for independence. You can explore local markets, interact with diverse communities from mainland India, and observe a unique blend of cultures. There's also the fascinating, albeit restricted, indigenous tribal heritage. In contrast, while the Maldives has a strong Islamic culture on its local islands (like Maafushi or Thulusdhoo), most resort tourists are largely insulated from it. Resorts are self-contained bubbles focusing on leisure rather than cultural immersion. You can visit Malé for a glimpse of local life, but it's often a fleeting stop. "Walking through Port Blair's markets and learning about the history at Cellular Jail gave the trip so much more depth than just pretty beaches." This cultural depth is a clear differentiator.

winnerSummary.why: The Andaman Islands provide a vibrant, accessible, and diverse cultural experience, including historical sites and local interactions, which is largely absent in the resort-focused Maldives.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Culture vultures, history enthusiasts, and travelers seeking authentic local interactions.

categories.title: 🌙 Nightlife & Relaxation
categories.summary: For sheer relaxation and curated evening experiences, the Maldives takes the lead. Resorts in the Maldives are masters of creating a tranquil, luxurious ambiance for unwinding. This includes world-class spa treatments, private beach dinners, sunset cruises, and sophisticated resort bars with live music or DJ sets. The focus is on serene privacy and pampering. The Andaman Islands, by contrast, have a very subdued nightlife. Most establishments close relatively early, and the evenings are typically spent enjoying quiet beachside dinners, stargazing, or simply relaxing. While places like Something Different on Havelock might have a mellow vibe, there are no bustling clubs or late-night bars. "After a day of diving, just chilling on our resort's deck with a cocktail, watching the stars over the ocean in the Maldives, was pure bliss." The Maldives offers a more refined and private relaxation experience, tailored for couples and luxury seekers.

winnerSummary.why: The Maldives excels at providing luxurious, private, and sophisticated relaxation options and resort-based entertainment, perfect for unwinding.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: Honeymooners, couples, luxury travelers, and those seeking ultimate tranquility and pampering.

categories.title: ☀️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both destinations share a similar 'best time to visit' window, primarily driven by their monsoon patterns, making this category a tie. For the Andaman Islands, the sweet spot is from October to May, with December to February being the peak season offering ideal temperatures (20-30°C / 68-86°F), calm seas, and excellent visibility for diving. The monsoons hit from June to September. In the Maldives, the dry season, running from December to April, is considered prime time, guaranteeing sunny skies, low humidity, and calm waters, which is perfect for enjoying the beaches and water activities. Expect hotel prices to be at their highest during these periods. The monsoon season in the Maldives typically runs from May to November. "Going to the Andamans in November was perfect, no crowds and the water was crystal clear; same for the Maldives in March." Planning around these dry seasons is crucial for both.

winnerSummary.why: Both destinations share a similar optimal travel window (roughly October/December to April/May) due to regional monsoon patterns, offering pleasant weather for tourism.
winnerSummary.who_this_matters_for: All travelers, as weather significantly impacts the enjoyment of these beach destinations.

verdict.summary: For adventurers seeking authentic experiences, pristine nature, and incredible value, the Andaman Islands are an undisputed winner, with daily budgets often under $70-$100 USD. If your dream involves unparalleled luxury, overwater bungalows, and a curated, pristine island escape, the Maldives is your splurge, expecting $300-$1000+ USD daily.
takeaways: Choose Andaman Islands: Choose Andaman Islands for an adventurous, budget-conscious trip focused on raw natural beauty, incredible diving, and a unique blend of Indian culture, ideal for backpackers, families on a budget, and those seeking active exploration.

Choose Maldives: Opt for the Maldives if you're chasing ultimate luxury, world-class resorts, absolute tranquility, and Instagram-perfect scenery, perfect for honeymoons, romantic getaways, or a no-expenses-spared pampering escape.

Choose Both: Consider doing both if you have 3+ weeks and a flexible budget; start with the cultural and adventure-rich Andamans for 7-10 days, then unwind in the Maldives for 5-7 days of pure relaxation, flying via Chennai/Bengaluru to Malé.

faqs.question: Which destination is better for a honeymoon?
faqs.answer: For an extravagant, private, and romantic honeymoon with iconic overwater bungalows and impeccable service, the Maldives is the undisputed choice. However, if you're a couple seeking adventure, cultural immersion, and incredible value, the Andaman Islands offer a unique and memorable romantic getaway without breaking the bank.

faqs.question: Are the Andaman Islands safe for solo female travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Andaman Islands are generally considered very safe for solo female travelers, especially in tourist areas like Port Blair, Havelock, and Neil Island. Locals are helpful, and crime rates are low. As always, exercise standard precautions, especially at night, but many solo female travelers report positive experiences.

faqs.question: What are the visa requirements for each destination?
faqs.answer: For the Andaman Islands, foreign nationals generally require an Indian visa. Many countries are eligible for an e-Visa. For the Maldives, most nationalities receive a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they have a valid passport, onward ticket, and sufficient funds. Always check the latest requirements for your nationality.

faqs.question: Can I find vegetarian/vegan food easily in both places?
faqs.answer: In the Andaman Islands, finding vegetarian and vegan food is very easy due to India's strong vegetarian culinary tradition. Most local restaurants and cafes offer numerous options. In the Maldives, resorts cater to international diets and can accommodate dietary restrictions, but local island cuisine might be more limited in vegan options; vegetarian is generally available.

faqs.question: Which destination has better snorkeling and diving?
faqs.answer: Both offer world-class snorkeling and diving with vibrant coral reefs and abundant marine life. The Maldives often has more easily accessible house reefs directly from resorts. The Andaman Islands, particularly around Havelock and Neil Island, boast incredible, less crowded dive sites and often offer more affordable diving certifications.

faqs.question: What's the wildlife like in each place?
faqs.answer: The Andaman Islands offer a rich blend of marine and terrestrial wildlife, including diverse bird species, wild elephants (on some islands), and saltwater crocodiles (caution advised). The Maldives is primarily known for its stunning marine life: sharks, rays, turtles, and countless reef fish, with very little terrestrial wildlife beyond birds and lizards.

faqs.question: Is alcohol allowed in both destinations?
faqs.answer: In the Andaman Islands, alcohol is freely available at licensed shops, bars, and restaurants. In the Maldives, alcohol is strictly prohibited on local islands due to Islamic law, but it is freely served within all private resort islands and liveaboards. Be mindful of local customs when visiting non-resort areas in the Maldives.

faqs.question: What are the major airports for each destination?
faqs.answer: The main airport for the Andaman Islands is Veer Savarkar International Airport (IXZ) in Port Blair, requiring a connecting domestic flight within India. For the Maldives, the primary international gateway is Velana International Airport (MLE) in Malé, which receives direct flights from numerous global cities.
